description: Differential-drive open-source ROS 2 robot by Ekumen (Ekumen-OS/andino, BSD-3-Clause). Values sourced from the official repo: wheel radius 0.0331 m and width 0.025 m, base 0.25 x 0.10 m (andino_description/config/andino/*.yaml); motors 2x DG01D-E gearmotors with encoders, rated 3-9 V (SparkFun), driven via L298N from the battery bus; battery 3x 18650 Li-ion cells (~11.1 V, holder per the official hardware BOM). Height and ground clearance are estimates (see the Robodex entry); battery capacity uses a typical 18650 cell rating, also an estimate — the BOM accepts any 18650 cells.

power (rail not specified in the data)

wiring.note: Andino's documented build, wired the standard way: the battery bus feeds the L298N driver (parts-catalog max 35 V in) and a 5 V buck converter — the catalog part whose stated job is powering 'the computer and logic from the main battery' — which feeds the Raspberry Pi 4 at 5 V. The Arduino Nano sits between the Pi and the driver and reads the motor encoders. Driver output to the motors is PWM: duty-limited, not a fixed rail, so that connection carries no voltage and is never voltage-checked. Voltages are the spec's battery voltage, the motors' recorded 3-9 V rating (SparkFun, via the official BOM) and catalog datasheet values; anything unsourced is 'not specified'.
